summary: Describes an allocation plan for IPv6 addresses to be used while testing prototype IPv6 software. It was an experimental arrangement meant for early test networks and was replaced by RFC 2471.

eli5.summary: Before a new playground opens, kids test the swings with pretend tickets. This set aside pretend addresses so developers could try out the new network without using real ones.

questions: how were early ipv6 test networks addressed
how did early ipv6 testing work
subtitle: Temporary address space reserved for IPv6 prototype development and testing.

tldr.problem: Developers building IPv6 prototypes needed real addresses to test the new protocol on experimental networks without consuming addresses from the production IPv6 address space.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1897 reserves a block of IPv6 addresses using a provider-based format where the registry ID is set to 11111 (binary), combined with autonomous system numbers and IPv4 addresses to create unique test addresses that can be assigned manually or via autoconfiguration.
tldr.outcome: This provided a safe sandbox for early IPv6 development. The addresses were temporary by design and were later replaced by RFC 2471 which used the documentation prefix instead.

facts.label: Address derivation
facts.value: Based on IPv4 addresses and AS numbers

today: RFC 2471 replaced this with documentation prefix addresses for IPv6 testing. RFC 1897 is now historical, remaining relevant only as documentation of early IPv6 development practices.

sections.title: Testing Addresses for IPv6
sections.content: IPv6 prototype developers needed a way to test their implementations on real networks without using addresses that might later be assigned for production use. RFC 1897 allocates a temporary block of IPv6 addresses specifically for this purpose. These addresses follow the provider-based unicast format and are temporary; all systems using them would need to renumber when IPv6 became standardized.
sections.eli5: When testing a new car on a track, you use test tags instead of real license plates so the numbers do not interfere with real cars on the road.

sections.title: Address Structure
sections.content: The test address begins with the format prefix 010 for provider-based unicast, followed by a registry ID of 11111 (binary) reserved by IANA for testing. The next field is an autonomous system (AS) number identifying the provider giving internet service to the tester's organization. The IPv4 network address field (24 bits) is derived from the testing organization's existing IPv4 address. A subnet ID and interface ID complete the address, allowing testers to build realistic address hierarchies on their test networks.
sections.eli5: The address is like a mailing label: 'test package', 'to provider AS 189', 'network 39.11.22', 'subnet 5', 'host 42'. Each part tells a router where the address belongs.

sections.title: Status and Replacement
sections.content: This Experimental protocol served its purpose during the early IPv6 development phase. RFC 2471 replaced it with a different approach using documentation address prefixes. By the time IPv6 became standardized, test address blocks like this one were no longer needed because official address allocation procedures were in place.
sections.eli5: Once the playground was ready, the testers went home and the real kids arrived. The pretend tickets were no longer needed because real playground rules had been decided.
